props.method: Thermodynamic equation of state (∂H/∂P)T = V - T(∂V/∂T)P summed over the components with the Berthelot equation of state and the critical constants; ΔHT,P° at 1 atm from Equation 9 at each temperature.

figure_1.text_value: ΔHT,P plotted against pressure (100-400 atm) for 25-900 °C

props.verdict: Figure 1 shows clearly a range of stable optimum working conditions.

props.name: 250 atm heat independent of temperature
props.statement: At about 250 atm the heat of reaction is virtually independent of temperature; fluctuations around a working temperature of 300 °C would produce little effect on the heat of reaction, so a process operated in this region may be more easily controlled.

props.name: agree with practical values
props.scope: comparison with values quoted in Dodge (ref. 2); the quoted values are not given
props.statement: The calculated values agree with values quoted (ref. 2) under practical conditions.

props.name: conversion increases with pressure
props.statement: Conversion increases rapidly with pressure: Kp' increases rapidly with pressure, and the effect is enhanced by the fact that Kγ' becomes smaller with increasing pressure.

props.name: equilibrium state pressure dependent
props.statement: Although the equilibrium constant Ka is a function of temperature only, the equilibrium state of the system is strongly dependent on pressure.

props.name: equilibrium unfavorable at high temperature
props.statement: Because the reaction is exothermic, the equilibrium becomes more unfavorable for methanol as the temperature increases.

props.name: ideal gas heat independent of pressure
props.statement: If ideal conditions apply, pressure will not affect the heat of reaction; at elevated pressures the conditions are not ideal and pressure will affect the heat of reaction.

props.name: keep temperature low
props.statement: The heat of the methanol reaction increases with pressure, and because the reaction is exothermic, by the Le Chatelier-Braun effect the temperature should be kept as low as is practical for a maximum yield of methanol.

props.name: thermodynamics predicts optimum
props.statement: The thermodynamic study should be useful for predicting optimum values of temperature and pressure for new processes and for checking operating conditions of existing processes.

props.name: hot spots in large converters may cause methanization
props.statement: In large converters with integral heat exchange systems, hot spots may develop in the catalyst mass and become hot enough (about 400 °C) to produce methanization, which may cause both product losses and enforce shutdown by converter runaway.

props.name: van der Waals treatment would give the Berthelot result
props.note: the derivation is in ref. (11), printed '(77)' in the text layer
props.statement: A general thermodynamic equation derived with van der Waals' equation, not used for the methanol calculations, should lead to the same result as the Berthelot equation.
